newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - May 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - May 26.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Deaths from diarrhoeal diseases rose to 23 in cyclone affected areas till Sunday, government officials said.
The standard of education in universities is showing a declining trend, according to the latest annual report of the Public Service Commission.
Peruvian Prtesident Alberto Fujimori said in Dhaka on Sunday that terrorism was a major impediment in the way of development and urged all democratioc states to stand up against terrorism.
About 200 Bangladeshi women and children are being smmuggled out of the country everyday, anti-trafficking activists told reporters on Sunday.
President Justice Shahabuddin Ahmed on Sunday summoned the parliament into session on June 10.
The government is planning to launch a low-cost housing project for the landless pople in the cyclone-prone coastal areas.
Disruption in gas supllies hit production in all the state-owned fertiliser factories during the current 1996-97 fiscal year ending June.
Chittagong Stock Exchange (CSE) has received seven offers from international vendors to implement its automation plan aiming to start screen based trading. REUTER
